sites.name: 8th Street School / West Gunnison Schoolhouse
overview: The surviving West Gunnison schoolhouse is the city's oldest standing public building and provides a clear Basic Scan identification target.

timeline.text: The surviving brick schoolhouse dates to Gunnison's early public-school era.

sites.name: Augusta Mine
overview: Augusta was the principal Poverty Gulch producer during the 1880s and is preserved as a named mine locality.

timeline.text: Augusta operated as a major high-elevation silver-era mine in Poverty Gulch.

sites.name: Black Queen Mine
overview: Black Queen was a productive Crystal-area silver mine represented by a documented shaft and related workings.

timeline.text: Black Queen formed part of the productive mining landscape serving Crystal and Sheep Mountain.

sites.name: Camp Bird Mine (Box Canyon District)
overview: Camp Bird is a distinct Gunnison County Box Canyon gold mine, separate from the famous Ouray County Camp Bird. Federal district reporting documents a two-compartment shaft, free-milling quartz ore, and wagon haulage to a 10-stamp mill below Bowerman.

timeline.text: USGS Bulletin 380 documents the Gunnison County Camp Bird mine in the Box Canyon district with shaft development and ore treatment associated with Bowerman.

sites.name: Carter Mine
overview: The Carter was a major Gold Brick district operation developed through a long tunnel system and linked underground workings.

timeline.text: Carter Mining Company developed extensive underground workings and later became one of Gunnison County's major operations.

sites.name: Erie Mine
overview: Erie was an important Tomichi/Whitepine replacement mine with documented lead-zinc-silver development.

timeline.text: Erie was developed and later operated under Callahan Zinc-Lead Company ownership.

sites.name: Forest Hill Mine
overview: Forest Hill is a documented Gunnison County polymetallic mine with repeated federal exploration work in the 1960s.

timeline.text: Federal exploration-assistance projects evaluated Forest Hill for precious and base-metal mineralization.

sites.name: Ida May Mine
overview: Ida May is a named Quartz Creek district mine with documented tungsten-era exploration.

timeline.text: Federal exploration records document a DMEA tungsten investigation at Ida May.

sites.name: Independence Mine
overview: Independence is a principal Box Canyon district gold mine. USGS reporting documents an approximately 80-foot shaft and two lower tunnels beneath the original ore lens, with later district records showing renewed 1930s production.

timeline.text: USGS Bulletin 380 and later Colorado district records document shaft-and-tunnel development and subsequent production at the Independence mine.

sites.name: Keystone Mine
overview: Keystone is a documented Gunnison County lead-zinc-copper mine with a mapped mine locality and mid-century federal exploration record.

timeline.text: Federal exploration records document work at Keystone for lead, zinc, copper, and silver.

sites.name: Lucky Strike Mine (Chance Area)
overview: Lucky Strike is a documented Gunnison County gold-led polymetallic producer with a traceable patented-claim group.

timeline.text: The Lucky Strike property incorporated several documented patented claims in the Green Mountain mining area.

sites.name: Pitkin Schoolhouse
overview: The Pitkin Schoolhouse is a surviving historic school building at 800 Main Street. State-register documentation identifies the wood-frame building as the only school serving Pitkin and the surrounding area from 1924 until 1962.

timeline.text: The present Pitkin Schoolhouse served Pitkin and the surrounding area as the community school.

sites.name: Raymond Mine
overview: Raymond was one of the larger Gold Brick district producers and was developed by a long adit cutting multiple veins.

timeline.text: Raymond developed an adit system extending roughly 3,000 feet through several mineralized veins.

sites.name: Sheep Mountain Tunnel
overview: Sheep Mountain Tunnel was a major Crystal-area mining venture directly tied to the powerhouse now known as Crystal Mill.

timeline.text: The Sheep Mountain Tunnel and Mining Company developed the tunnel and used the nearby powerhouse to support underground drilling and ventilation.

sites.name: Smith Opera House / Grand Apartments
overview: A surviving 1882 building that briefly housed the Smith Opera House before long adaptive reuse.
